I. Our Three Measures Are Text‐Supported  
  1. “Primitive Surface Pretence”  
    a. Concealment of the true civilization  
       – <quote>"They mustn't suspect the existence of  the city underground or we're finished before we've started."</quote> (p. 38) – Only the beggar and a few “actors” go topside; the bulk of Snaddrath remain hidden.  
       – <quote> Except the beggar. Beggars went barefoot. </quote> (p. 24) – Only a designated outcast appears on the surface; genuine citizens never expose their air‐cars or technology.  
    b. Suffering hardship to maintain “primitive” illusion  
       – <quote> Beggars went barefoot. Beggars suffered. </quote> (p. 24) and “teeth chattered… the rags…joyously making their way through the demolished wires” (p. 31) – They willingly endure discomfort so Terrans believe in the savagery of Snaddra.  
       – <quote>all have to go live out on the  ground during the day, like—like savages."</quote> (p. 20) – Even Bbulas frames it as “necessary,” showing full commitment to the charade.  
  2. “Primitive Accommodations”  
    a. Rapid construction of rudimentary huts and ceremonies  
       – <invalid_quote>“We have prepared our best hut for you…run up in only three days.”</invalid_quote> (p. 33) and “this very evening…a rain dance” (p. 40) – Hasty, ramshackle structures and rituals tailor‐made to match Terran expectations of primitive cultures.  
    b. Deliberate abandonment of advanced transport and materials  
       – <quote> air-cars and  self-levitation were on the prohibited list as being insufficiently  primitive.
</quote> (p. 31) – They voluntarily eschew their own technology to lend authenticity to the primitive setting.  
       – Bbulas’ injunction: <quote>try to look hungry, and remember this isn't for you or for me, but for Snaddra."</quote> (p. 31) – The objective is deception for the planet’s survival, not comfort or genuine primitiveness.  
  3. “Acting Uninfluenced by Terran Culture”  
    a. Banning all visible imports  
       – Cloth, contact lenses, metal underskirts concealed; “woven metal” garments only (p. 32–33) – They hide evidence of imports and advanced craft.  
       – <quote> it was not politic for the Earthmen to discover how heavily the  Snaddrath depended upon imports.
</quote> (p. 33) – Explicit policy of concealment.  
    b. Use of broken, “primitive” language patterns  
       – Skkiru’s “broken Inter‐galactic” (p. 31) instead of fluent Terran to maintain the pretense of linguistic backwardness.  
       – When Terrans speak their own tongue, they are “shhh”ed: <invalid_quote>“Shhh…Don’t be so impatient!”</invalid_quote> (p. 41) – Secrecy until rapport is irreversibly established. If genuine communication were desired, they would flaunt, not hide, their fluency.  

II. Rebuttal of Debater_B’s Claims  
  1. “They live primarily underground; only beggars appear topside.”  
    – Debater_B concedes “fight…to live belowground” (p. 1) and “had actually touched it only when taking off and landing” (p. 30). If they truly “lived” on the surface, they would expose more than a single beggar. The rapid construction of huts for visitors further shows these are temporary “sets,” not genuine dwellings.  
  2. “Use of Terran language is only for advanced study, not rapport.”  
    – If the goal were to “establish undue rapport,” why hide their native fluency? Their entire program is to force Terrans to “soften up” after observing extreme primitiveness. They fear “self‐preservation” forcing true rapport only “later,” once the Terrans are committed: <invalid_quote>“We hope…to soften them up…But why only the beggar wears mudshoes?”</invalid_quote> (p. 41). This staged deception demonstrates that initial “broken” speech is integral to the primitive façade.  
  3. “Terran influence in tapes and blueprints is concealed, not genuine.”  
    – These imports are carefully hidden. The library fictapes disturb Skkiru as “corrupting” (p. 19) and Bbulas takes measures to suppress evidence. The viewer is never allowed to see cloth, metal, or advanced maps; instead we see mud, scant clothing, and rain‐dance ceremonies. The irony of “antique blueprints” emphasizes their inferiority and impracticality. If genuine Terran influence ran the show, they would employ proper plans and dismiss the “primitive” overtness.  

III. Why Our Interpretation Best Explains Textual Consistency  
  1. The “Anthropological Deception” Motif  
    – <invalid_quote>“Our old culture…too much like the Terrans’ own to be of interest…only primitive societies…differ sharply…and we have to be different to attract Earthmen.”</invalid_quote> (p. 36) – Snaddra’s very survival hinges on appearing “primitive.” This consistent theme of deception runs from secret underground cities to the enforced beggarhood of Skkiru.  
  2. Reluctant Suffering and Desire to Return  
    – Skkiru’s personal agony and hope for alternate solutions (pp. 32–33) reveal that neither he nor any Snaddrath wish to remain “primitive” permanently. Their tragic love story and Bbulas’ “pension” fears underscore the charade’s unpleasantness. Genuine primitiveness would not provoke such yearning for true culture.  
  3. Temporal Constraints of a Charade  
    – They plan only “for this visit”: “We promise to make our intensive analysis…as painless as possible. We wish only to study…not to tamper.” (p. 41). They anticipate departure. If real rapport or “assimilation” were desired, they would not entrust only flimsy huts and mud‐shoes to preserve their species. The rain dance itself is a device to shorten rain‐ridden stays: <invalid_quote>“But why do you want rain?…It is a dance to stop rain.”</invalid_quote> (p. 40). They simply wait for conditions that permit “taking off and landing” again.  

Conclusion  
Every measure—surface pretence, primitive huts, tabus on imports, “broken” speech—is part of a unified stratagem of temporary façade designed to attract, detain briefly, then release Terran anthropologists so that Snaddra’s true society remains concealed and can continue surviving underground. Debater_B’s insistence on “speaking Earth’s language” and “hiding spaceships” misunderstands the text’s repeated emphasis on broken speech, concealment of all advanced gear, and Skkiru’s personal torment at being forced into beggarhood. Our answer harmonizes all narrative elements, whereas theirs requires ignoring key passages. Accordingly, the correct measures are those we have outlined.
